Bobby Jones. An American amateur golfer whose dominance in the 1920s and early 1930s established golf as a major spectator sport and created the template for amateur excellence. His achievements with 13 major championship victories, all as an amateur, remain the gold standard for amateur achievement in a professional era.

He won 13 major championships while strictly amateur: 7 US Opens, 5 British Opens, and 1 US Amateur, a feat never matched by an amateur. In 1930, he achieved the Grand Slam, winning all four major championships in a single calendar year—a record that stands unmatched. At the height of his dominance, he retired from competitive golf at age 28 in 1930 to pursue law and focus on his family. Never playing professional golf, remaining strictly amateur throughout his career, was extraordinary for a player of his dominance.

Co-founding the Masters Tournament in 1934 at Augusta National Golf Club gave the sport one of its most prestigious events. Jones inspired a national obsession with golf during the 1920s and 1930s, making the sport a mainstream American pastime. Later he became a golf course designer and was instrumental in the formation of the United States Golf Association, extending his influence on the sport far beyond his playing years.
